editorial:
Imagine you are working your tail off at a high-pressure ad agency, but your boss thinks you are too young and flighty to handle a big promotion. That is exactly where you find yourself as the main character in this flick. To prove you are a responsible adult, you make a snap decision to lie and say you are engaged. The problem is, you are totally single. You end up hiring a handsome stranger to play your fiancé, and suddenly your professional life and your fake love life start to crash into each other. It is a lighthearted ride that captures that frantic feeling of trying to keep a huge lie going while hoping you do not get caught.

You will really enjoy the chemistry between the leads, as they make the fake relationship feel believable and sweet. The pacing is snappy, though some of the plot twists are a bit predictable. If you love rom-coms from the 90s, this is a great pick for a cozy night in. You should definitely try renting it on Apple TV or streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to get the best picture quality. If you are a fan of physical media, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your collection is a smart move for a movie this charming.
endingExplained: In the end, the lie finally falls apart, but it leads to a moment of truth. The main character realizes that her boss's approval is not as important as being honest with herself. She admits the fake engagement was a sham, but she discovers that her feelings for the fake fiancé have become real. They decide to give a real relationship a try, and she finds a better balance between her career and her personal happiness.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic romantic comedies and stories about fake relationships.
